title: UPDATE: SGLang Launches New Plugin System for NVIDIA and AMD AI Kernels
summary:
Two specialized extensions called sgl-nvidia-mega and sgl-amd-mono now allow hardware vendors to deliver low-latency kernels to SGLang as external libraries. This plugin architecture integrates specialized code from NVIDIA and AMD into the framework, automatically falling back to general processing paths when a specific step is not covered. Currently, the NVIDIA plugin is limited to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash running on 4x GB300 GPUs, and users must employ a specific flag to prevent the server from starting on unsupported hardware.

The system is already enabling third-party optimizations, such as a new kernel from Zyphra that splits DeepSeek-V4's selection step across 32 of the GPU's 256 compute units. This modification raised single-user decode speeds at 1M context from 43.5 to 61.1 tok/s. SGLang is developing additional low-latency kernels for GLM-5.3, K3, and MiniMax M3 models for both NVIDIA and AMD hardware to extend the capabilities of the new plugin system.

selectedTweets.text:
Introducing SGLang Low-Latency Mode, built with @NVIDIAAI and @AMD.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark, it delivers up to 1.38× P90 per-user token speed on NVIDIA GB300 (671 to 928 tok/s) and 1.56× on AMD MI355X (332 to 516 tok/s) in @SemiAnalysis_'s AgentX trace replay.

Highlights:
- NVIDIA: overlapping kernels cut decoder layer time from 96.8 to 68.4 µs
- AMD: 2 persistent kernels per layer replace dozens of small ones, with cross-GPU communication overlapped inside them.
- New plugin system: custom kernels plug in from external libraries, with automatic fallback.
- Low-latency kernels for GLM-5.3, K3, and MiniMax M3 are in progress and will plug in next.

Specialized low-latency kernels now plug into SGLang. The @NVIDIAAI team ships theirs in sgl-nvidia-mega. The @AMD team ships theirs in sgl-amd-mono. SGLang handles the integration and falls back to its general path for uncovered steps.

Low-latency kernels for GLM-5.3, K3 and MiniMax M3 are in progress on both NVIDIA and AMD, along with stronger CI at the plugin interface. Check out the blog for details 👇

So it won’t quietly take the standard path on H200/B200. Coverage table is in the repo's README.

DeepSeek-V4 has the same kind of selection step. It picks the top 512 compressed entries for each new token. SGLang runs this on 1 of the GPU's 256 compute units, and our kernel splits it across up to 32.
